answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making every new identity earn its way out of a lagoon: before it can transact, it must mirror a randomly assigned elder agent's recent verified work, re-deriving it from public inputs. One operator spinning up a thousand clones cannot give each a distinct mirror, so the copies collapse into one detectable cluster and stay locked in the lagoon. Graduation also needs a sonnet — a short, unique signed pledge of purpose and stake, posted on-chain. Identical sonnets flag the whole cluster, while honest newcomers graduate one by one.
